# [Baseline] - WIN - U - Microsoft Outlook Cached Mode Managed

Turns on Cached Exchange Mode for the user's own mailbox and keeps everything shared out of it: shared mail folders, shared calendars and Public Folder Favorites are not copied to the OST file.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | own baseline |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Outlook_Cached_Mode_Managed.json`](Baseline_WIN_U_Microsoft_Outlook_Cached_Mode_Managed.json) |

> One of three variants on the same axis — assign one, never two: this one, Cached Mode Default (cached mode on only) or Cached Mode Off (Online mode). The user's own mailbox is cached, so Outlook works offline and searching is local. What is attached to it is not: a shared mailbox added to the profile is the main cause of OST files of tens of gigabytes, and reading it online is no practical loss. Note the polarity of the two shared folder settings, which run opposite to each other: *Disable shared mail folder caching* set to **Enabled** writes `cacheothersmail=0`, and *Download shared non-mail folders* set to **Disabled** writes `downloadsharedfolders=0`. Both zeros mean do not cache. Applies only to classic Outlook (the Win32 app from Microsoft 365 Apps); the new Outlook for Windows does not read these ADMX settings and has no OST. The well-known slider **amount of mail to keep offline** (3 months / 12 months / all, registry value `SyncWindowSetting`) is *not* in the settings catalog: the ingested `outlk16v2` ADMX has eighteen settings under *Cached Exchange Mode* and that slider is not one of them. Anyone who wants to set it can only do so via a custom ADMX import or the Office Cloud Policy Service — so outside this baseline.
